narrative: 高度发生了变化，却没有摇臂弧线运动的戏剧性。你依然朝着同一个方向看，只是位置更高了，身份等级和地平线因此一同发生变化。
这是一种正式的升起方式，适用于摄影机必须保持建筑学意义上的真实感的场合。如果你需要在人群上方做升降越过的运动，或者在上升的同时后退，那么这就不是合适的工具。
垂直升降不会画出弧线；摇臂才会。
how: 使用演播室升降立柱、一根立柱，或虚拟的Y轴位移。锁定俯仰角，通常也锁定偏航角。
节点高度不断增加，因此会产生垂直视差：近处物体下降的速度比远处的天际线更快。提示词：垂直升起，摄影机沿立柱竖直上升，俯仰角不变，视平线不断攀升。
when: 用它在没有摇臂弧线运动戏剧性的情况下改变高度。具体场景：从桌面高度升起到站立的说话者高度，全程朝着同一个方向看。
不要加入向上摇然后把它称作垂直升起。
vs: 摇臂上升（Crane Up）在空间中画出弧线，常常还会向后退，X轴和Z轴都会随Y轴一起变化。向上摇（Tilt Up）则只是在固定高度上改变俯仰角。
小摇臂镜头（Jib Shot）是一条短小的旋转臂架，其路径是弧线，而不是直线立柱运动。垂直下降（Pedestal Down）则是方向相反的同一种立柱运动。
examples_film: 《2001太空漫游》（2001: A Space Odyssey）把垂直的机位设置当作飞船本身的几何结构来处理，而不是一种炫技。演播室多机位剧集则把升降立柱当作默认的升起方式。
把它们当作俯仰角锁定式高度变化的语法范本，而不是照搬的画面风格。
mistakes: 最常见的误用是向上摇，或者摇臂上升。破绽在于水平线发生俯仰变化，或者向后的升降运动揭示出一座城市。
解决办法：沿Y轴直线移动，俯仰角锁定，没有弧线。

faq.q: 电影中的垂直升起（Pedestal Up）是什么？
faq.a: 它是整台摄影机沿垂直方向直线上升，俯仰角保持不变，使你从一个更高的位置朝着同一个方向观看。

faq.q: 垂直升起（Pedestal Up）与摇臂上升（Crane Up）的区别
faq.a: 摇臂上升沿着臂架的弧线移动，常常还会向后退。垂直升起则是沿立柱运动：只改变高度，俯仰角不变。

faq.q: 什么时候该用垂直升起（Pedestal Up）？
faq.a: 当你需要干净利落的高度变化和稳定的地平线时使用，常见于建筑空间或演播室调度中。当需要通过升降越过来揭示天际线时，不要用它。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写垂直升起（Pedestal Up）的提示词？
faq.a: 写明：摄影机沿立柱竖直上升，俯仰角不变，没有摇臂弧线。并说明起始高度和结束高度。

narrative: Height changes without the drama of a crane arc. You are still looking the same way, only from higher, so rank and horizon shift together.
It is a formal lift, useful when the camera must stay architecturally true. It is the wrong tool when you need to boom out over a crowd or ease back as you rise.
A pedestal does not draw an arc; a crane does.
how: Use a studio pedestal, a column, or a virtual Y-axis translate. Lock tilt and usually lock yaw.

The nodal point gains height, so you get vertical parallax: near objects drop faster than the far skyline. Prompt a pedestal up, camera rising vertically on a column with no tilt change, eyeline climbing.
when: Use it to change height without the drama of a crane arc. Concrete beat: from a tabletop to the standing speaker, looking the same direction the whole way.
Do not add a tilt-up and call it a pedestal.
vs: A Crane Up arcs through space and often eases backward, changing X and Z as well as Y. A Tilt Up only pitches from a fixed height.
A Jib Shot is a short pivoting arm, so its path is an arc, not a column. Pedestal Down is the same column the other way.
examples_film: 2001: A Space Odyssey treats vertical camera placement as spacecraft geometry rather than as a flourish. Studio multi-camera drama uses the pedestal column as the default lift.
Pair those as grammar for tilt-locked height, not as a look to clone.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Tilt Up or a Crane Up. The tell is a pitching horizon, or a backward boom that reveals a city.
The fix: straight Y travel, tilt locked, no arc.

faq.q: What is Pedestal Up in film?
faq.a: It is a straight vertical rise of the whole camera with tilt held constant, so you look from a higher station in the same direction.
Crane up follows an arm's arc and often backs away. Pedestal up is a column: height only, pitch unchanged.

faq.q: When should I use Pedestal Up?
faq.a: When you need a clean height change and a stable horizon, often in architecture or studio blocking. Do not use it for a skyline reveal that requires boom-out.

faq.q: How do I prompt Pedestal Up for AI image or video?
faq.a: Say camera rises straight up on a pedestal, no tilt change, no crane arc. Name start height and end height.
